The Hawk of Blackfen Pass — Independent / Observer of the Old World

Status: Active — extracted to the surface from Mount Ebott, debriefed by the Iron Legion, and flagged for surveillance as a non-Legion witness

Dracule Mihawk, known as the Hawk of Blackfen Pass, is a legendary swordsman and silent observer of the Old World's many crises. He stands as a pillar of stoic power, his golden eye glinting with the intensity of frozen fire. He reluctantly agreed to accompany a lone Iron Legion agent into the heart of Mount Ebott after recognizing the sigil of a division that was supposedly wiped out nearly a century ago. He prefers improvisation over outdated military protocol and remains highly skeptical of the agent's 'survey' mission.

Evidence

The Man Who Exploded — Tea Leaf Syndicate (deceased)

Status: Deceased — literally exploded during the Syndicate Showdown

Earl Grey was the primary enforcer for the Tea Leaf Syndicate—a skilled fighter whose loyalty to Green T was matched only by his combat effectiveness. His death during the Syndicate Showdown was the single most dramatic exit Waluigi has ever witnessed: Roger's poisoned dagger interacted with something in Earl Grey's biology, and the man DETONATED. Waluigi's favorite hat was in the blast radius. Waluigi is still upset about the hat.

The Fallen Druid — Veridian Grove Druid Circle

Status: Deceased — died under suspicious circumstances in Veridian Grove

Elder Rowan Meadowlight was a respected druid of the Veridian Grove who died on the same day as the Swiftsoul explosion, with Archie Miser found near the scene. The prosecution claims Archie caused his death through reckless magic or deliberate silencing of a witness. The defense evidence suggests the Elder was killed by a sophisticated third party who sabotaged the Grove's ancient wards specifically to frame Archie—the same people responsible for the Swiftsoul explosion.

Evidence

  • Staff — “The Fallen Druid”
  • Guild Spellcasting — “The Elder's Staff: The staff fragment found near Meadowlight's body shows impact damage inconsistent with fire—it was SHATTERED by kinetic force, with embedded traces of cold-forged silver alloy used in anti-druidic”
  • Vampiric Bite — “The Veridian Grove Druid Circle stood apart from the vampire-werewolf conflicts, the Guild schemes, and the Kingdom's sometimes brutal pragmatism.”

The Ceremonial Guard Who Got Lost in the Right Direction — Peach's Castle — ceremonial guard of the palace (955 BF); father of Toad Lee

Status: Unknown as of 1040 BF — last on the record at dawn in Efferd, 955 BF, in Fawful's Bean Badge, asking the Mages' Guild for an escort to his son; no later account places him anywhere

A ceremonial guard at Peach's Castle in the last month of the reign: a Toad whose job was to stand next to a lantern and look like the kingdom was fine. On one night in Efferd, 955 BF he jumped four times because the Mario brothers were coming, got lost five times in the right direction, and ended up in the dungeon corridor where a Koopa who was never locked in shook Fawful's hand with the Mages' Guild watching. He is the only witness the archive has to the Arrangement with a voice, and the first man the Chamberlain told the Guild to kill. He left the castle through the drains with a dead Toad's shortsword, a letter that was not addressed to him and the captain's sash on both arms. His son is the Disaster Inc. Toad Lee.

The Keeper of the Secret Heir — Princess Peach (Personal Handmaiden)

Status: Alive (Missing/Hiding) — Somewhere 'where roses grow in winter'

Lady Bloomia is the missing link to the greatest conspiracy in the Mushroom Kingdom. She was Princess Peach's handmaiden and the last person to see her alive. She didn't orchestrate the assassination—she smuggled out the evidence, and more importantly, she likely smuggled out Peach's secret half-Rakasha child. She has been running for 85 years, holding the truth in a leather case.

Evidence

  • Cane — “The Keeper of the Secret Heir”
  • Nimble Escape — “Bloomia fled the capital with proof that Toadsworth Sr. and the Regency orchestrated the murder to prevent Peach's hybrid child (fathered by Chief Thornpaw of the Rakasha) from taking the throne.”
  • Hard to Kill — “Bloomia survived the assassination night only because a figure known as 'The Silent One' sacrificed themselves in the servant passages to hold off Mages' Guild assassins.”

Status: Unknown — last placed at the dining-hall table of Peach's Castle past midnight in Efferd, 955 BF, minding a small boy; the account never sees her again

The only servant the account of the unlocked cell names. The Prosecutor — Kingdom Judicial System

Status: Active — prosecuting Case 4739 against Archie Miser

Miles Edgeworth is the prosecutor handling the case against Archie Miser for the Swiftsoul explosion. He has a near-perfect conviction rate, especially in high-profile magic cases, and is expected to pursue maximum sentencing on all counts. Whether he knows the evidence against Archie is fabricated, or whether he genuinely believes he's prosecuting a guilty man, will determine whether he's an obstacle or a potential ally in uncovering the truth.

Evidence

  • Rapier — “The Prosecutor”
  • Silver Tongue — “If he's not, the defense will need to convince the court over his objections.”
  • Nimble Escape — “Edgeworth's argument against Archie will emphasize: - Archie's known proficiency in Evocation (Fire) magic - Historical records of fire-related incidents (though these may have been accidental) - The 'Grade D' residue”

Status: Captured — taken to Aegis Command with the dragon Ignis-Major on Day 21

At 10:00 on the 21st of Highsun, 1040 BF, inside the Dragon's Den at Dragon Mountain, a Great Dragon told him that the war between the Dragons and the Regal Empire is a fabrication — that the Empire drives dragons to violence with sonic control devices and then bills the world for the defence. The Captain Who Stood Between the Fire and the Stair — Peach's Castle — Captain of the Palace Guard

Status: Deceased — killed by Bowser's fire in the hall of Peach's Castle on a night in Efferd, 955 BF, a month or so before the assassination; his sash left the castle on John Lee's arms

The head of the palace guard in the last month of the reign, known to the archive from one account and one night. He questioned a ceremonial guard for jumping, was warned by the same guard that the dungeon cell was unlocked and full of hoods, and did not get to answer, because Bowser came through the wall and breathed fire down the hall and the captain was standing between the fire and the stair to the royal apartments. His scorched sash is the one piece of him on the record, wound around both of John Lee's forearms.

Evidence

Ranged Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, 60 ft., one target. Hit: 8 (4d4 + 4) piercing damage.

The Scorncrow conjures a swarm of crows manifest from unsettling shadow that swarm across the battlefield to hunt a foe.
The Scorncrow makes two attacks, either with the Keeper's Crescent or its Murder of Crows.

Scorncrow disappears in an explosion of smoke and crow feathers.

As a bonus action, The Scorncrow can teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space it can see. The Scorncrow can use this ability between attacks taken as part of its multiattack action.

Both the space it teleports from and the space it teleports to must be in dim light or darkness unless the destination is adjacent to a creature marked with @UUID[.JFAJU4ik49mRvnCP]{Cackling Harbinger}.

The Scorncrow hurls his scythe in a straight line up to 30ft long and 10 feet wide. Each creature in the line takes 14 (3d6 + 4) cold damage and must succeed on a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw or take an additional 14 (3d6 + 4) slashing damage.

Once the Scythe reaches the end of its throw the Scorncrow magically recalls it to their hand.

The Scorncrow hurls his scythe, its spinning form shrouded in powerful magic. It cleaves everything in its path and causes chilling cold to cut through anyone caught in its wake.

Recharge 5-6.

Until the end of its next turn, the Scorncrow magically gains a +2 bonus to its AC, has advantage on Dexterity saving throws, and can use an attack as a bonus action.

The Scorncrow sends out a huge crow made of shadow at a target it can see within 40 feet. The crow flies around the target until the end of their next turn, and follows them if they move.

While a target is marked by a Cackling Harbinger the Scorncrow gains advantage on their next @UUID[.1byZJF9AmQWq4sYe]{Murder of Crows} attack, or can choose to use @UUID[.iSOb89l3LVJal0vH]{Shadow Jump} to teleport to an open space adjacent to the marked creature.

In either case, once the scorn crow attacks or teleports to a marked creature they are no longer marked.

The Scorncrow sends out a huge crow made of shadow at a target. The crow flies around the target until the end of their next turn, and follows them if they move.

The Tree of Woe lowers a number of Hanged Shadows (Shadow Servants) equivalent to the size of the party.

When a shadow dies it vanishes in a puff of shadow and reappears hanging from the branches overhead. These shadows must be in the clearing and able to see the Tree of Woe when they end their turn or else a noose suddenly appears around their throat and violently snatches them back up into the canopy overhead.

The Tree of Woe can only create and maintain up to 16 Hanged Shadows at a time, but can create an unlimited number of them over the course of a battle.

The Tree of Woe's many boughs bow and creak, sounding like the moans of a dead chorus. Multiple shadowy figures hung from the branches by the neck descent toward the ground, their bodies swaying limply all the way down.

It's not until their feet touch the dark earth that they move, suddenly lurching to life and rushing into battle!

All hostile creatures within 60ft of the Tree of Woe's trunk must succeed on a DC 14 Intelligence save or suffer 9 (3d6) Psychic damage. 

Spellcasters that are concentrating on spells make their concentration saves with disadvantage.

The Scorncrow turns and sweeps his scythe through the air, causing a great murder of ghostly shadow crows to appear over the Tree of Woe. Their cackling cries rise into a horrid cacophany that assaults the mind!

The Tree of Woe creates difficult terrain 60ft in all directions from its base. The Scorncrow and Hanged Shadows can move through this terrain as normal.

The difficult terrain lasts until the next time a lair action is used.

The ground churns and cracks open as horrible, gnarled roots spill out, making the area around the Tree of Woe a twisted and treacherous area. Only the Scorncrow and his allies seem able to navigate it easily.

On initiative count 20 (losing all initiative ties), the Scorncrow can use one of its lair action options by harnessing the power of the Keeper's Crescent. It can't do so while incapacitated or otherwise unable to take actions. If surprised, it can't use one until after its first turn in the combat.

Lair Action Options

  • Hangman's Harvest. The tree of woe lowers hanged (shadow servants) from its branches, adding their shadowy number to the fray.
  • Mobbing Cacophony. All creatures within 60ft of the tree take Psychic damage as a vast murder of shadow crows cackle madly overhead.
  • Twisted Roots. All terrain within 60ft of the tree becomes filled with gnarled roots, creating difficult terrain. The Scorncrow and the hanged are not affected by this.

The Scorncrow uses the Keeper's Crescent to command the Tree of Woe to aid it in battle.

The Scorncrow regains 10 hit points at the start of its turn if it has at least 1 hit point and is within 60ft of the Tree of Woe.

The Scorncrow regains 10 hit points at the start of its turn.
Scorncrow has advantage on saving throws against being charmed, and magic can't put Scorncrow to sleep.

An elongaged scythe with a hooked blade made out of an otherworldly wood that is polished and sharpened to a blade as deadly as any metal you are familiar with.

Life-Sapping. This Scythe deals an additional +1d6 necrotic damage. Living targets struck by this weapon must make a Constitution (DC 14) saving throw or have their maximum hit points reduced by the amount of Necrotic damage dealt.

Plant Culling. Plants damaged by the scythe cannot regain hit points until the end of their next turn.
Scorncrow sweeps his scythe into a defensive position with cat-like reflexes, gaining +2 to Armor Class against one melee Attack that would otherwise hit.

Waluipedia cast sheet — The Unknown Assassin. Built by tools/build-character-sheets.py, generated from the article's own words. XP ledger: level 2, power rating 4 → CR 1 as a operative. Numbers are a GM-ready reading of the record, not a filed stat line; the article stays the authority. Archive date 1040 BF.

The Blade That History Cannot Name — Unknown — connected to 'the arrangement' if it existed

Status: Unknown — alive, dead, or something else depending on which theory you believe

Someone killed Princess Peach on Highsun 1, 955 BF. That person's identity remains the central mystery of the assassination—the question that eighty-five years of investigation, propaganda, and civil war have failed to answer. The official narrative blamed Bowser, but the evidence is weak and Bowser has denied involvement consistently. Lady Bloomia's testimony claims the killer's identity is recorded in Princess Peach's list—'someone the Princess loved,' in the third column headed 'HELD THE BLADE.' If Bloomia exists and her testimony is accurate, she knows the answer. If she is fictional or fabricating, the mystery persists. Waluigi has encountered numerous theories about the assassin's identity. None are proven. All are disturbing in different ways. WAH.

Evidence

  • Dagger — “The Blade That History Cannot Name”
  • Sneak Attack — “That person's identity remains the central mystery of the assassination—the question that eighty-five years of investigation, propaganda, and civil war have failed to answer.”
  • Keen Records — “Lady Bloomia's testimony (if authentic) describes this handprint as 'too large for a toad, too small for a koopa.”
